text:
anya: Quick question — when a user saves a per-route console view that includes a model filter, should the saved view persist the routing hint (e.g. route_policy) or just the model filter?

mike: I vote both. If we don't persist routing hint, savedviews could be nondeterministic during rollouts. Need a way to recreate the exact signal used in the original analysis. :thinking_face:

sasha: +1 on deterministic. downside: if you persist a Dedicated-only route_policy and a non-admin loads it, they'll hit a permission/capacity mismatch. We should store the policy id but surface validation when opening.

kevin: Proposal: saved_view schema includes { filters, pinned_models, route_policy_id | "auto", scope }. Example payload: 

```json
POST /api/console/saved_views
{
  "name": "High latency - model-x",
  "scope": "route", // route | project | global
  "route_id": "route_abc",
  "filters": [{"field":"p95_ms","op":">","value":500}],
  "pinned_models": ["model-x:hash"],
  "route_policy_id": "policy_123" // optional, null => use current routing rules
}
```

oliver: UX note: show a tiny badge next to the saved view list item when a policy is pinned: "policy: policy_123" with tooltip "This view will attempt to route to policy_123. If you don't have access, a fallback will be used." Also add an affordance "Change route policy" in the header.

anya: Telemetry point: we also need to emit which saved view was used for telemetry/ cost-estimates. Otherwise cost preview numbers don't match what users saw when saving.

mike: Suggest event: saved_view_opened with fields (view_id, route_id, model_ids[], sampling_rate). Example: 

```json
{
  "event": "saved_view_opened",
  "view_id": "sv_789",
  "route_id": "route_abc",
  "models": ["model-x:hash"],
  "telemetry_sample_rate": 0.02
}
```

sasha: Edge case — inherited/global savedviews that apply across routes. A team might save a global filter "error_rate>1%" that should be run against many routes but models pinned per-route differ. We need scope + per-route overrides.

kevin: Implementation sketch for DB columns: id, owner_id, scope (route|project|global), scope_target_id (nullable), payload_json, pinned_policy_id (nullable), allowed_models (json array), created_at. When resolving a view at runtime: if pinned_policy_id exists, validate access; if invalid, fallback to policy resolution policy = "best_compatible" and emit a resolved_policy_id in telemetry.

oliver: UI: when saving, show a dropdown for "Scope" and a small inline check for "Pin routing policy" (optional). If pin chosen, show a permissions check and a warning: "Pinned policy may not be available to all viewers." :warning:

anya: Can someone draft the minimal API contract for the save endpoint so I can run it past security (saved views may include model pin metadata we need in audit logs)?

mike: Happy to. Draft: 

```http
POST /api/console/saved_views
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string (optional)",
  "scope": "route|project|global",
  "scope_target_id": "route_abc or project_xyz (nullable)",
  "filters": [ {"field":"string","op":"string","value":"string"} ],
  "pinned_models": ["string"],
  "pinned_policy_id": "string (nullable)",
  "visibility": "private|team|org",
}

Response 201 { "view_id": "sv_..." }
```

anya: Perfect — I'll take that to SecOps. Also, @rollout-bot can we schedule a quick canary for the UI changes early next week?

rollout-bot: Canary scheduled: console-savedviews-policy-badge (canary-1) -> deploy queued for 2026-03-23 03:00 UTC.

oliver: I'll mock up the badge and the save modal today and drop a Figma link. http://internal/figma/savedviews-badge

sasha: Thanks — next steps: (1) API contract review with security, (2) telemetry events added to schema, (3) small UX mock & perms check. We can fold into the next patch release. :+1:
